title: Section 6: SSRF guard in is_valid_fetch_host is correct and should be defended
description: peer_fetch.rs:59-222 is_valid_fetch_host() allows only Tailscale CGNAT range (100.64/10) for IPv4 and ULA (fc00::/7) for IPv6, plus explicit .ts.net/.tailscale.net hostnames. It rejects all RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, and public internet addresses. This is a correct conservative SSRF defense: a malicious peer cannot redirect blob fetches to internal services or the public internet. A future contributor might want to allow arbitrary IP or hostname — that would be wrong. The tight allowlist is the security property.
